# Corrective Requirements Checklist: Git-native Grove

**Purpose**: Reviewer-owned requirements-quality gate for the bounded Phase 9 corrections **Created**: 2026-08-22 **Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `$speckit-checklist` workflow based on feature context and requirements. **Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied. **Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement completeness

- [x] CHK001 Are readable default trunk-path requirements defined for initial and additional managed trunks without reintroducing a persisted live trunk inventory? [Completeness, Spec §FR-010, §FR-018A-B]
- [x] CHK002 Are collision, truncation, case-folding, native ref-byte, and valid v1 suffix-preservation requirements all addressed for trunk allocation and observation? [Coverage, Spec §FR-006A-C, §FR-010, Decision 003]
- [x] CHK003 Are linked advisory-base requirements complete for local, configured remote-only, absent, and ambiguous preferred trunks while forbidding local trunk creation? [Completeness, Spec §FR-011D-E, §FR-020]
- [x] CHK004 Are point-of-use requirements defined for pending-operation ownership, stale registrations, detached reachability, checkout cleanliness, and relocated filesystem targets? [Completeness, Spec §FR-021-FR-026, §FR-034B-FR-036]
- [x] CHK005 Are FR-039A–FR-045 unambiguously retired as historical citation keys, with foreign-schema refusal defined by live FR-046 and no pseudoref/bundle/loader work left in the execution plan? [Completeness, Spec §FR-039A-FR-046] — **Resolved 2026-08-24:** active artifacts now implement constitution 5.0.0's no-migration boundary.

## Requirement clarity

- [x] CHK006 Is the exact ordinary trunk outcome objectively stated as `trunks/main@<repo>` rather than only “under the trunk layout”? [Clarity, Spec §FR-010, §003-git-native-grove-SC-016]
- [x] CHK007 Is the collision suffix rule clear about when a suffix is required, what byte identity derives it, and what observed Git fact remains authoritative afterward? [Clarity, Decision 003 §Decision]
- [x] CHK008 Is lexical/canonical path mismatch distinguished from a simple escape and assigned one unambiguous pre-mutation result? [Clarity, Spec §FR-012D]
- [x] CHK009 Is “current operation target” defined sufficiently to prevent replay against a stale pre-relocation absolute path or a later unrelated occupant? [Clarity, Spec §FR-021, §FR-023]
- [x] CHK010 Are successful worktree-add/restore postconditions measurable through exact common-directory, HEAD/branch, and clean-status facts? [Measurability, Spec §FR-021, §FR-036]

## Requirement consistency

- [x] CHK011 Are Decision 003, the v2 §5 naming contract, v3 config contract, proposal, data model, quickstart, and acceptance scenarios consistent about readable trunk paths? [Consistency, Decision 003, Spec §FR-010]
- [x] CHK012 Does linked remote-tracking base resolution remain consistent with the prohibition on linked trunk refs/worktrees and Git's ownership of live refs? [Consistency, Spec §FR-001, §FR-011D-E]
- [x] CHK013 Do target-lock requirements cover create, remove, restore, and reconcile with compatible identity keys while preserving Grove-lock-only concurrency claims? [Consistency, Spec §FR-021, §FR-025]
- [x] CHK014 Is valid bare-repository/worktree Git topology distinguished from forbidden legacy ownership parsing, without preservation bundles or reparenting? [Consistency, Spec §FR-046, Decision 001] — **Resolved 2026-08-24:** schema-3 acquisition recognizes Git topology independently from foreign ownership state.
- [x] CHK015 Do deterministic target-order and stable-reason requirements agree across command, result, and recovery contracts? [Consistency, Spec §FR-032A, §FR-033A]

## Acceptance criteria quality

- [x] CHK016 Can every accepted corrective finding be mapped to a red executable witness, one implementation task, focused verification, and a fresh adversarial disposition? [Traceability, Tasks §T091-T096] — **Resolved 2026-08-24:** T091–T094 and round-5 R5-F1–F3 each have an observed red state, bounded correction, focused/full green verification, and independent post-fix disposition; both post-review P2 proof/documentation advisories were also closed.
- [x] CHK017 Does prior-release parity require an exact preserved/superseded disposition and named assertion witness for every inherited scenario rather than scenario-ID presence or aggregate counts? [Acceptance Criteria, Spec §FR-051A, §003-git-native-grove-SC-015-SC-016]
- [x] CHK018 Is the `TRUNK-01` witness specified strongly enough that replacing the readable path assertion with an opaque path makes the traceability gate fail? [Measurability, Spec §003-git-native-grove-SC-016]
- [x] CHK019 Is foreign-schema refusal measurable through zero mutation plus exact running-version, executable-path, encountered-schema, and accepted-schema facts? [Measurability, Spec US6, §FR-046] — **Resolved 2026-08-24:** the void bundle criterion is no longer treated as release work.
- [x] CHK020 Is corrective convergence quantified as no unresolved P0/P1/P2 bug or proof-gap finding within at most five rounds? [Acceptance Criteria, Spec §003-git-native-grove-SC-015]

## Scenario and edge-case coverage

- [x] CHK021 Are normal, collision, truncation, contained-symlink, escaping-symlink, non-UTF-8, and historically allocated trunk-path scenarios explicitly covered or intentionally refused without reading legacy ownership state? [Coverage, Spec §FR-006A-C, §FR-010, §FR-012D, §FR-046]
- [x] CHK022 Are stale-recipe cases defined for unregister, alias reuse with a different stable ID, changed common directory, changed OID, occupied target, and hook-dirtied checkout? [Coverage, Spec §FR-012B, §FR-017, §FR-036]
- [x] CHK023 Are recovery exception paths defined for workspace relocation, old-path reoccupation, target ownership by another operation, and unreachable detached commits? [Coverage, Spec §FR-021-FR-026, §FR-034B]
- [x] CHK024 Are schema-1, schema-2, unknown-schema, and malformed-schema inputs explicitly refused before legacy field interpretation or mutation? [Edge Case, Spec US6, §FR-046]
- [x] CHK025 Are equivalent selector-order permutations and stable refusal propagation included in deterministic result requirements? [Coverage, Spec §FR-032A-FR-033A]

## Scope and assumptions

- [x] CHK026 Is the corrective scope explicitly limited to demonstrated redesign bugs, regressions, and proof gaps without adding commands, storage domains, or product capabilities? [Scope, Plan §Phase 9]
- [x] CHK027 Is local macOS release evidence distinguished from inherited runtime constraints without adding CI, Linux-specific verification, or Windows support? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions, Plan §Technical Context]
- [x] CHK028 Are historical green review/release reports clearly superseded so they cannot conflict with the current corrective gate? [Consistency, Reviews] — **Resolved 2026-08-24:** the prior release audit and Phase 9 analysis retain their historical results but now carry explicit supersession markers naming T090/T095.
- [x] CHK029 Is it explicit that tests-first corrective work preserves partial artifacts/refs and never uses compensation or destructive cleanup? [Consistency, Spec §FR-022-FR-025, §FR-035]
- [x] CHK030 Are unsupported concurrency guarantees excluded while immediate revalidation and honest conflict reporting remain mandatory? [Boundary, Spec §FR-021, §FR-025-FR-026]

## Requirements-quality convergence audit — 2026-08-24

- [x] CHK031 Are all live migration statements in the user story, plan, quickstart, data model, traceability map, tasks, and production checklist explicitly reconciled with constitution 5.0.0's no-migration rule? [Conflict, Constitution VI, Spec §FR-039A-FR-045]
- [x] CHK032 Is the release verification venue stated consistently as local macOS across the constitution, spec assumptions, plan, validation guide, and tasks, with CI/additional-platform work excluded? [Conflict, Constitution 4.0.0, Spec §Assumptions]
- [x] CHK033 Is the release traceability obligation stated in a way that can be completed within the approved bug-fix scope, without silently introducing a new evidence architecture? [Scope, Ambiguity, Spec §FR-051A-B] — **Resolved 2026-08-24:** T089 permits missing obligations in existing live rows and stronger already-cited witnesses, but forbids product behavior, schema, counting-rule, validator-architecture, and assertion-local claim-model changes.
- [x] CHK034 Are historical release reports required to carry an explicit supersession marker whenever later evidence invalidates their terminal PASS claim? [Consistency, Gap, Reviews]

## Structural output-parity correction — 2026-08-24

- [x] CHK035 Is no-migration support treated as settled scope, with Decisions 001–003 limited to schema-3 topology/schema concerns and no live README/help/provenance promise of a migration command? [Consistency, Spec §FR-046, §FR-049C]
- [x] CHK036 Does output parity cover every registered command through one source-architecture invariant rather than a hand-selected list of command assertions? [Coverage, Spec §FR-033B-C, §003-git-native-grove-SC-017]
- [x] CHK037 Is the parity requirement structurally enforceable by prohibiting independent human callbacks/direct handler writes and deriving both serializations from one complete structured value? [Measurability, Spec §FR-033C, Contract V3OUT-03]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied.
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation.
- `$speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers.
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `$speckit-specify` and `$speckit-clarify`.
- Add comments or findings inline.
- Link to relevant resources or documentation.
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference.
